> They are at, their heart, opposites. In other words, the sci-fi action comedy comes down to taking extraordinary situations and playing them in a comedic deadpan way. The high school comedy is taking very recognizable genre situations and going over the top with them.

The form of the sci-fi action is a pretty standard buddy cop set up but in a sci-fi world. The veteran actor is the straight man, the younger actor is the eccentric funny one. One's more by the book, the other is more of a rebel. Things can only be played as deadpan as they are because the younger actor's reactions aren't. He's a fish out of water reacting to a world that he doesn't understand and a lot of the jokes are playing off that.

Meanwhile the joke in the high school comedy is that it's *meant* to be a recognisable genre situation but that real high schools aren't anything like they are in movies anymore. The jock actor is the jock, the nerd actor is the nerd, but the world has changed so much that now the nerd is cool and the jock is an outcast. They're not really going that far over the top, more of the jokes are about unpicking and parodying the situations that the producer seems to think they're playing off of.

In other words, both movies are about rookie cops being dropped into a world they don't understand and a lot of the jokes are coming from the same place. So it's totally doable, you just need to cast both the nerd actor and the jock actor in the younger actor role (new recruits in the sci-fi action) and then have a straight man (in the high school comedy it's the veteran actor). From there the set up is pretty much identical to the first sci-fi action, and to the high school comedy. Same basic character archetypes in the same basic plot structure.
